page: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for accelerated matrix operations.

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. For local storage, it bundles 480 GB of Premium Storage-capable local capacity. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not provide any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The high 4.2 GHz clock speed drives strong single-core metrics, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2138.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression performance. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks are relatively weak, with stress-ng multi-core performance and large-block memory read/write speeds falling into the poor category. Consequently, this server is best suited for workloads that benefit from high single-thread performance and local storage capacity, such as lightweight database operations, basic file processing, and single-threaded application tasks.
